independentNeed: A make-to-order production run has to let the business say whether the ordered goods physically exist in the completed quantity, separately from the instruction that asked for them and from the record made about them, because a delivery commitment made on a record that runs ahead of physical reality is a false promise. Separately, the stocking side has to keep the stock record in agreement with what physically arrived. Each of the two needs stands on its own.

in: one make-to-order production run of one finished item
the separation of work instruction, physical manufacturing, physical confirmation and the completion record
taking released goods in charge, checking them against what production confirmed, putting them into stock, recording the stock movement and state
out: work-in-progress costing and production scheduling / MRP
quality-management-system detail and lot / batch traceability

sourceBackedFacts.text: Manufacturing instruction, material issue, warehouse stock movement / stocktaking and shipment appear as cross-subsystem business concerns.
Material receipt and issue, manufacturing completion and shipment are physical / external-world pressures.
More than one responsibility context exists in such a business.
The instruction / entry stage and the actual change of stock or accounting are not necessarily simultaneous.
Manufacturing instruction, physical manufacturing / completion, recording the completion in the system, and shipment work do not necessarily fold into one system command.
Inventory distinguishes the actual movement (receipt / issue) from the history and stock state that follow it.

teiOriginalDecisions.text: The production run is one procedure with its own need: it must keep physical completion apart from the instruction and from the record.
Instruction, physical manufacturing, physical confirmation and the completion record are four separate steps; no single step both confirms and records.
Stocking is a separate procedure with its own need and a separate candidate responsibility context.
Physical confirmation (production side) and the arrival check (warehouse side) are verification of external state; they use the observation-boundary realization and carry no Observation identity.
Releasing confirmed goods is the last act that production performs with the goods; taking them in charge is where the receiving responsibility starts.

crossViewQuestions.question: At each moment, which quantity does the business treat as authoritative for finished goods that can be committed to delivery: the recorded completion, the physically confirmed quantity, the quantity taken in charge, or the resulting stock state, and which responsibility owns each?
Which of these steps could be realized by an Application interaction at all, and which are manual or physical and lie outside any Application?

handoff.basis: The two procedures have independent needs and different responsibility contexts, and accountability for the goods and their count belongs to production until the receiving responsibility takes them in charge. That change of accountability is Business meaning of its own and is not implied by the order of steps.
conditionIsNot: a restatement that the previous step finished
